articles.title: 2020 - Murder at the Kalyvia Health Centre: 'He Put a Spell on Me and I Was Losing Weight.'
articles.author: Ανώνυμος Συγγραφέας
articles.excerpt: A shocking murder case motivated by beliefs in magical practices that led to a tragic end.

image.alt: Crime scene at the Kalyvia Health Centre

content.value: The 32-year-old perpetrator was taken before the examining magistrate after confessing that he had murdered the 60-year-old employee of the Kalyvia Health Centre. In his confession, he stated that he believed the victim had placed magical spells on him causing weight loss.

The case was particularly difficult due to the victim's blameless life, having never provoked any reactions in the community. Investigators from the Homicide Division conducted a thorough inquiry, managing to locate the perpetrator in an isolated village in Albania, despite the fact that he had no previous connections to that country.

The crime was committed a few days before the holidays, in the underground car park of the health unit. The 60-year-old was found dead with gunshot wounds to the head and chest, before he even had time to leave his vehicle.

The key to the case was the reconstruction of the perpetrator's movements. Police officers identified the purchase of an illegal weapon from a criminal group in Menidi, while also establishing his flight to the Albanian border. Cooperation with Albanian authorities led to his definitive arrest.

seo.metaDescription: A 32-year-old murdered a Kalyvia Health Centre employee in 2020, believing he had put a spell on him causing weight loss. Arrest in Albania.

articles.title: 2014 - Satanist Human Sacrifice in Glyfada: The 22-Year-Old's Manifesto
articles.author: Ανώνυμος Συγγραφέας
articles.excerpt: A shocking case of ritual murder by a young man who identified as a Satanist.

image.alt: Crime scene in Glyfada - Satanist ritual

content.value: The 22-year-old Alexandros Papageorgiou confessed on May Day 2014 to the murder of a homeless woman in the central square of Glyfada, carrying out ritual acts of a Satanist character. The perpetrator appeared to embody forms of contemporary Satanism through online activity.

Digital traces that remain: YouTube searches for 'approaching Satanist circles', a comment with his full name and phone number on a Rotting Christ video (the song 'Kata Ton Daimona Eaytoy'), and a public call for initiation into Satanist practices two months before the crime.

The ritual dimension was revealed by: self-inflicted cuts in blood on his hand, an inverted cross and the number 666 on a public bench, use of a stone as a sacred instrument of death, and the deliberate choice of the date (Easter) followed by a plan for a second sacrifice during the summer solstice.

The police investigation focused on: 1) Genetic material from bloodstained soil 2) Digital footprint on social media 3) Psychiatric history of the perpetrator (reported disorders from adolescence). The victim was identified as a 57-year-old homeless woman with a 15-year history of homelessness.

The judicial aftermath: The Lamia Court of Appeal imposed a sentence of 14 years' imprisonment despite reactions to the light sentence. The decision was met with protests from the victim's family, who denounced the inadequacy of the legal system.

The Ioannina Security Police arrested them, also uncovering a case of antiquity trafficking at their home in Perdika, where various ancient objects and religious relics were found.

Interesting finds included voodoo dolls with photographs of victims, books on black and white magic, as well as archaeological objects such as coins from the Roman, Byzantine and Ottoman-Turkish periods.

The private investigator Giorgos Tsoukalis, who played a discreet role in the investigation, expressed satisfaction at the successful conclusion, noting his surprise at the existence of Satanist practices in our day and age.

articles.title: The Satanists of Pallini (1991 - 1993)
articles.author: Διάφοροι Συγγραφείς
articles.excerpt: Complete timeline of the Satanists of Pallini case: from Satanic rituals to releases from prison. Analysis of crimes, court decisions and social reaction.

image.alt: Photographic material from the trial of the Satanists of Pallini

content.value: Founding and Ideological Background

In December 1991, the 19-year-old Asimakis Katsoulas and the 15-year-old Dimitra Margeti, who were already studying books on black magic, held their first ritual at Katsoulas's home, marking the genesis of a 'group' of Satanist activities in Pallini.
Soon the 17-year-old Manos Dimitrokalis joined them, with whom secret initiation rituals for young high school students were organised, under the promise of initiation into Satanism.
The Murder of Dora Syropoulou (27 August 1992)

On 27 August 1992, the 14-year-old Dora Syropoulou disappeared after school and was found dead at the site of Sesi Grammatikou, strangled, sexually abused and doused with petrol, in a horrific 'sacrifice' to Lucifer.
The Murder of Garyfalia Giorga (14 April 1993)

On 14 April 1993 (Holy Wednesday), the 28-year-old mother of two and hotel employee Garyfalia Giorga stopped at a traffic light; the perpetrators, posing as police officers, forced her to board, and after transporting her to a factory and then to Sesi, strangled her and struck her on the head with a stone.
Discovery of the 'Crypt' and Arrests (30 December 1993 – 1 January 1994)

On 30 December 1993, officers of the Greek Police discovered an underground crypt in Peania containing wax effigies of people, pinned photographs and a 'book of rituals', among which was a photograph of the basketball player Panagiotis Giannakis.
The following day (1 January 1994) Katsoulas, Margeti and Dimitrokalis were arrested, following Dimitrokalis's remorseful confession to a priest on New Year's Eve.
Trial and Convictions (23 June – 1 July 1995)

The trial was held at the Athens Mixed Jury Court, with charges of co-perpetration of homicide, impersonation of a public official, illegal detention, abduction of a minor, desecration of religion and formation of a gang for the commission of felonies.

On 27 June 1995, the prosecutor recommended the maximum sentences; on 1 July 1995 the court sentenced Katsoulas and Dimitrokalis to double life imprisonment plus a lengthy custodial sentence, and Margeti to imprisonment of 17 years and 4 months, with the mitigating circumstance of post-adolescence applied in her case.
Appeals and Upholding of Sentences (December 1997 – January 1998)

At the Athens Court of Appeal (Korydallos) on 8 and 24 December 1997 the first-instance decisions were unanimously upheld, while a third appeal was rejected on 17 January 1998, securing the original sentences.
Releases and Public Reaction (2001–2016)

23 November 2001: Dimitra Margeti was released under restrictive conditions (reporting to the Pallini Police Station, prohibition on leaving the country), following a decision of the Piraeus Council of Misdemeanour Judges.
March 2014: Manos Dimitrokalis was released having served three-fifths of his sentence, under Article 105 of the Penal Code.
December 2016: Asimakis Katsoulas was released after 23 years of imprisonment and numerous parole applications.

image.alt: Crime scene with a skeleton at Agios Athanasios

content.value: On an uninhabited island belonging to the Niarchos family, opposite Itea, a skeleton was discovered buried near the surface (depth <30cm) beneath a layer of rubble. The forensic investigation in Lamia revealed gunshot wounds and signs that the body had been transported from another location.

The interest of the case is heightened by the discovery of charred remains and human bones believed to be connected to ritual practices. Local sources refer to long-standing activity by groups practising alternative worship methods on the island.

The investigation identified three main lines of inquiry: 1) Identification of the victim 2) Origin of the gunshot wounds 3) Connection with the observed magical rituals. Despite the island being privately owned, there were no surveillance systems to record activities.

articles.title: 1989 - The Slaughterer of Patisia: Slaughter Over a Broken Engagement
articles.author: Ανώνυμος Συγγραφέας
articles.excerpt: A tragic case of double homicide with folkloric elements of magical practices in Attica.

image.alt: Crime scene in Patisia - The case of Niki R.

content.value: The case of the 45-year-old Niki R. is a combination of patriarchal social norms and folk magical beliefs. The motive for the double murder (1989) stemmed from the breaking of an engagement with Grigoris Papadatos, where the perpetrator believed that the victim's sister had been magically incited against her.

Key ritual elements: The use of three lit candles as a symbolic element in a melting spell, the choice of a darkened room for ritual actions, and the symbolic connection of the melted wax with the 'wasting' lives of the victims.

The police investigation revealed: 1) Anthropological analysis of hair (DNA 1989) 2) Traceological examination of blood-stained shoes 3) Psychological profile of the perpetrator with a history of unresolved crimes. The murder weapon — a butcher's knife — was never recovered.

The legal proceedings made history with: a violent incident during the trial where a relative of the victim attacked the perpetrator, interrogation techniques that extracted a full confession, and a final conviction to double life imprisonment by a Mixed Jury Court.

articles.additionalNotes: The case was adapted as a television film under the title 'Magic Love' in the series 'The Anatomy of a Crime'

image.alt: Police officers in Heraklion outside a house

content.value: The grandson of the 85-year-old woman found yesterday hacked to death at her home in the Poros area of Heraklion is said to be the perpetrator of her murder.

During the preliminary investigation the 25-year-old kept falling into contradictions and eventually, according to reports, confessed to being the perpetrator of the atrocious crime, claiming according to the same reports that she had put a spell on him!

It was he himself who notified the police about the crime; he had been living with her recently and was taken to the Heraklion Security Sub-Directorate, as he had been the focus of police investigations from the start.
Acquitted: the 25-year-old who killed his grandmother in Heraklion
The Trial

The 25-year-old's rambling testimony before the Heraklion examining magistrate lasted almost two hours. 'Have you repented of your deed?' the magistrate asked him. 'Of course not. I did what was right. I saved myself and my family's lives. She intended to kill all of us,' said the young man.

The court acquitted the 25-year-old who had been accused of murdering his grandmother a year earlier in Poros, Heraklion. However, the court decided that the 25-year-old would continue to be hospitalised at the PAGNI psychiatric clinic.

articles.title: 2024 - Imathia: Husband of 37-Year-Old Requests Investigation into Black Magic — Accused Appears Before Magistrate for the Murder of Her 6-Month-Old Baby
articles.author: Σύνταξη parapolitika.gr
articles.excerpt: The husband of the 37-year-old accused of murdering their 6-month-old baby in Imathia requests an investigation into her possible involvement in black magic.

content.value: The estranged husband of the 37-year-old K.G. suspects even the possibility of black magic, after the woman on the afternoon of last Tuesday, in a state of amok, brutally beat and fatally wounded their barely six-and-a-half-month-old baby boy in Macrochori, Imathia.

The second husband of the woman and father of the wrongfully slain infant is sunk in grief following the loss of his child, as well as the attacks he is receiving from the accused's family, yet he is determined to go on the offensive.
The man in question appears shaken by the testimony of the neighbour who snatched the baby from her hands.
We note that the 37-year-old said to him with cynicism, referring to her baby: 'Don't worry, it's a vampire. If you put a little blood on it, it will recover.'
On behalf of his client, the father's lawyer Stelios Sourlas announced that he will request an investigation into the mother's involvement in black magic.

'We will request an investigation into any possible involvement of the mother with black magic, following what was heard and the testimonies that she called the child a vampire who would drink blood and return to life,' he stated, and also explained that the baby's father had feared for his own life too, which is why he left the house: 'He feared that at some point she might suffocate him in his sleep at night, she threatened him and hit him. From September he had seen his child three or four times.'

The estranged husband of the 37-year-old himself spoke to ANT1 on the programme 'To Proino' about the alleged abusive behaviour of the perpetrator: 'She killed our baby because she wanted to take revenge on me, to punish me, because I left the house last August, because I couldn't take it any more. She was pathologically jealous, searching phones and Facebook, making scenes and outbursts out of nowhere. She would hit me, slap me, squeeze my throat, but I never reacted. I never hit her. On the contrary, she falsely reported me for domestic violence to punish me and make me run to the courts,' said the baby's father, who claimed to have photographs showing marks from the blows.

At the same time, however, he claimed to have also faced hostility from his in-laws: 'I asked my in-laws for help and received worse treatment. They insulted me and slandered me. Saying I was to blame for everything. I had no idea that this woman had psychological problems. They had hidden from me that she had been hospitalised in a psychiatric clinic,' he noted.

We note that the prosecutor has pressed criminal charges against the 37-year-old for intentional homicide, with the accused — a nurse by profession — having been given a deadline to date to give her statement to the examining magistrate.

articles.title: 1977 – 'Satan Made Me Do It' – The Murder of Tatsopoulos with 26 Adze Blows
articles.excerpt: Account of the horrific spousal murder of Sotiris Tatsopoulos by his mentally ill wife Eleni, who claimed she was acting under the influence of Satan.

image.alt: Front page of the Eleftheria newspaper - 23.02.1977

content.value: Athens, 22/2/1977 - The wife-killer Eleni Tatsopoylou, 47 years old, who on Sunday night killed her husband by crushing his head with an adze, was brought before the Public Prosecutor.
The prosecutor characterised the offence as intentional homicide, committed in a particularly heinous manner, and with the formed case file, referred her to a regular examining magistrate.
To the journalists who approached her, she began to speak as if hypnotised, gazing at the ceiling: 'Without wishing to, I hit him. I feel remorse for hitting my Sotiris.'
In response to related questions, she answered in the same tone: 'No, he was not unfaithful. No, I was not jealous. No, we never quarrelled. We were always loving.'
'Then why did you kill him?' was the question. She opened her eyes wide and, full of surprise, said: 'Good heavens! I killed my Sotos? No, no, that's not true.'
'Don't you realise that you struck him 27 times with the adze?' the journalists asked her. 'No, no. I only hit him twice,' she replied, 'and those times without meaning to.'
To her lawyer, who sat beside her and advised her to request an extension from the examining magistrate, the wife-killer was heard to say: 'I give you my word, I have never committed another crime.'

The chronicle: On Sunday, around 7 in the evening, Eleni Tatsopoylou, 47 years old, from Stratinitsa in Ioannina, killed her husband, Sotirios Tatsopoulos, 63 years old, from Constantinople, a painter and decorator.
The crime took place in Amfithea, at 29 Othonas Street, where the couple lived in a three-room house.
Eleni Tatsopoylou was Tatsopoulos's second wife, following the death of his first. She herself had been hospitalised in a psychiatric hospital in 1959.
This was concealed by her family — perhaps because they believed Eleni was now well — and so the marriage took place in 1969.

For the first three years of their marriage she showed no sign of anything. They lived harmoniously. The only thing she told him was that nightmares tormented her and that she believed that malicious people, who did not look kindly on their marriage, had put a spell on them.

It seems that he too believed it — or pretended to — so as not to displease her. And this appears most likely, because she would say that her husband always listened to her and never denied her wishes.
He would listen to her, therefore, and they both went to magicians and witches to have their 'spell lifted'. The sorcerers told them that they could see bad signs upon them.
They saw blood on Tatsopoulos's feet, and on his wife's hands.

These 'prophecies' of the sorcerers strengthened her thoughts and she would tell him: 'You see how they want to harm us? They want to kill us. I'm telling you the truth. Be careful not to let them harm you. Don't trust anyone.'
He would try to reassure her, telling her that they were protected by Saint Nicholas and Saint Anthony, which they had in their home.
However, after three years, her condition worsened and Tatsopoulos was forced to put her in a clinic in Glyfada.
She stayed there for about 20 days and came out with the doctors' confirmation that she was well, but also with the statement that she had to follow a specific course of treatment.

They gave her some medicines, which she was supposed to take regularly. But she did not want to follow the doctors' instructions, because she considered the medicines too to be the work of Satan — i.e. of the Devil — who, as she said, was tormenting her.

The Devil, as she said, appeared to her and pushed her to do evil. When they asked her — both her husband and her family — whether he appeared in her sleep or when she was awake, she replied: 'When I'm awake.'
Her family tried to persuade her that these were in her imagination and nothing more. 'No,' she insisted, 'I see him clearly and it is Satan.'
'And what does he look like?' they asked her. 'I don't know,' she replied. 'It's a shadow, something like a cloud that takes the form of Satan and tells me to do evil.'
But she, as she said, did not want to do evil — especially to a person she loved and had no complaint about.
Her sisters told their brother-in-law to be careful. He in turn did everything he could to keep her happy. He never contradicted her, because by then he understood her condition.
She herself had no complaint about anything — even in sexual matters, as she said, and she said it repeatedly, both to her sisters and to acquaintances and friends of theirs.
On Sunday she was fine, and they both set out at midday and went to a relative's house. They returned around 6 in the afternoon.
Tatsopoulos was tired, got changed, put on his pyjamas and lay down, telling her to come and lie down with him. She told him to lie down and that she would come when she had done some chores.
He fell asleep with his head against the wall. She — as she said — was pacing around the house. She was restless, because the idea that Satan had put in her mind was tormenting her.
She sat beside the stove, on top of which — as she claims — stood the icons of Saints Nicholas and Anthony (which, as it turned out, did not exist there; she imagined them).

The shadow of Satan appeared and began to tell her: 'What did I tell you to do? Why are you protecting him? He is to blame for everything. Only by getting him out of the way will you find your peace. He did the same things to his first wife — he tormented her and killed her.'
'But he has done nothing bad to me,' she replied. 'Listen to what I tell you,' Satan answered her.

And then, no longer knowing what she was doing, she went to the kitchen, opened a drawer and took the adze. As he lay there with his head turned toward the wall, she delivered two blows with the back of the adze.
He woke up, jumped out of bed and ran toward the bathroom. There, from the blows he had received, he collapsed.
Seeing him fall, she said to him: 'Now you will pay for Eleni too' (the name of his first wife was also Eleni). And she began to hit him with the adze on the head, until she smashed it.
'Don't ask me, I can't remember how many times I hit him,' she said after the discovery of the crime.
The head of the Forensic Services established 25 blows and 2 initial ones. So many had the unfortunate man received that his head was pulped.
After her terrible crime — of which, due to schizophrenia, she had no awareness — she locked the door of the house and stayed all night with her dead husband in the bathroom, sleepless.

At around 9 in the morning, without changing her clothes and without shoes, she went to the police station and told the duty officer that she had killed her husband, adding: 'Satan made me do it. I saw him clearly and he told me to kill Sotos, my husband. And I killed him.'

And indeed, a little while later, they were confronted with the horrific scene. Police Director Mr. Moutzouridis and Police Superintendent Tsanakis arrived on the spot, followed by the head of the Forensic Services, Mr. Panos Giamarelos.
Mr. Giamarelos established that the crime had been committed with extraordinary fury. He examined the killer and determined that she was a schizophrenic with no awareness of her criminal act.
She recounted the circumstances under which she committed her crime with indifference — as if it were not she who had killed her husband.
And when Mr. Moutzouridis asked her why she had done it, she replied: 'Satan made me. I saw him, alive and in the flesh, and he told me to kill Sotos, my husband. And I killed him.'

articles.title: The Bloodshed for the Heart and Income of a Notable Medium 1934
articles.excerpt: Shooting in Metaxourgeio: the cousin-pursuer insists on separating the medium Androniki from her husband; she had foreseen the bloodshed. The perpetrator surrenders, the victim fights for his life.

image.alt: Bloodshed for the heart and income of a notable medium (1934)

content.value: The strange causes of a shooting near Metaxourgeio — Forcibly to separate his cousin from her husband and make her his mistress — The coveted 'Medium' foresaw the bloodshed — Strange information.

An unusual-for-our-times drama of honour unfolded yesterday from Metaxourgeio on Kolonou Street. Unusual because the fatally wounded — struck by 5 bullets from the conjugal Browning (a type of firearm) — was the would-be lover, or rather the forced lover of his married cousin. She had been giving him financial help out of family obligation, and he demanded love in return. He was expelled, he struck and was struck, he grew angry and began walking naked in the yard — as a nudist or, as one great writer of centuries past gave the psychiatric science cause to define a specific type of schizophrenia: 'exhibitionism' — and finally he met the conjugal revolver.

And the first bullet — another diabolical coincidence, as the forensic report establishes — found him in the place that was goading his abnormal passion. The drama has a very strange aspect for those who are not acquainted with the psychic mysteries.

The apple of discord, the wife, is one of the stars of the Society for Psychical Research, as Mr. Tanagras also confirms, and she had foreseen the shooting. While conversing with two of her clients — as they themselves confirm, Mr. M. Niforatos and Mrs. Anthi Georgopoulou — she was suddenly seized by dizziness.
'Blood! Giorgos and Panagis are rolling in blood! The army! The police!'
Twenty-four hours later, indeed, Giorgos and Panagis were rolling in blood, and one was taken by the police and led to the cells, while the other was taken to hospital, where he died.

But let us introduce the characters of the drama before we reach the events themselves. She is called Androniki, née Valsamatou, originally from Cephallonia. She is approximately 35 years old with chestnut hair and a gleam in her eyes that all those who engage with spiritualism have. Three years her junior, her husband G. Mazarakis — a sturdy man with a thick moustache, a thoroughbred Cephalonian type. He is a grocer by trade; at least that is how he justified having the revolver on him. He bought old revolvers and rifles, repaired them and sold them on.

And the third, a troublesome man, slightly younger than his adversary, also Cephalonian, a driver by trade which he did not practise every day. The police, and specifically the 6th police precinct of the area, had already recorded many incidents involving him: brawls in various places, thefts, and one conviction for which the police had been searching for him for several months.

With 'psychic' Androniki, his cousin, he had become acquainted only 2 years earlier. He was completely unemployed at the time, and Androniki's mother happened to meet him on the street one day and invited him to their home for a meal. He was the son of a cousin of hers and the woman decided she ought to care for him. The introductions were made at the house on Kerameikos Street.
'Your cousin!'

They showed him affection — both she and her husband — as they would any poor relative. They dressed him well and assigned him a role as housekeeper. He cleaned and tidied the house, because Androniki, especially in the evenings, received — owing to her psychic abilities — a large and distinguished clientele.

About Androniki's psychic abilities, Angelos Tanagras had written an article in his magazine and in the newspapers. He has classified her in the category of mediums who self-hypnotise while awake. She gives descriptions of persons and things at a great distance with mathematical precision. She also has intuitions, terrifying ones; among other things, we have been informed that she had foreseen the suicide of a very wealthy man — a well-known and cheerful figure of Athenian high society who had wished to marry her.

She had also foretold the accident of the doctors returning from hunting the previous year, with such precision that one of the relatives of the deceased had called her 'a woman of the devil'. She had discovered her abilities at a young age and with their proper cultivation was considered by Mr. Tanagras to be one of the foremost mediums.
Since, therefore, she was doing well and earning quite a bit of money, Nikolatos had apparently set his sights on the income from her work.
The Attacks

A few months after settling in her home on Kerameikos Street, he began his amorous advances. Androniki, when she realised he was not joking, told him to leave the house, threatening that if he did not leave she would inform her husband of the whole situation. However, he not only did not leave the house, but when he saw that his cousin had said nothing to her husband, one afternoon he literally attacked her. Due to her resistance and the screams heard by her sister, the sexual assault was averted. Despite this, he told acquaintances of his — and others who had gathered outside in the courtyard while she was still screaming — that he had achieved his aim.
'Let her scream, I got what I wanted.'

The 'psychic' was then forced to tell her husband roughly what had happened. 'I told him first,' she says, 'to throw Giorgos out of the house and then to cut off contact with him.' The perpetrator, who was fond of the victim, asked what had happened. She then told him what had occurred, after making him give his word that there would be no incident. That same evening, Nikolatos's belongings were thrown out of the house. But what the husband did not learn from his wife, he learned from the man himself.
'I'll take your woman whatever you do.'

The two men came to blows, but were separated by the neighbours and the police arrived. But he refused to leave and the intervention of a prosecutor was requested. Eventually, five months earlier, the couple moved to 39 Kolonou Street, where the drama took place yesterday. Even with the move, the harassment did not stop, as Nikolatos would go to the house when the husband was away and cause scenes. A little while later, he rented the ground floor room of the building and settled in there. From then on, there were continuous quarrels in which the police were often called. The most serious incident occurred a short time ago, when Nikolatos discovered that Mazarakis had a relationship with a widow. He considered it the right opportunity to break up the couple, while also striking the perpetrator's head with a bludgeon.
The Bloodshed

Nikolakos, as he had done on other occasions, was wandering around half-naked in the common courtyard, making gestures that cannot be described, while those around him called for him to go inside. His response was to make a corresponding motion. The two women entered their home beside themselves.

That morning, the intuition of Androniki had preceded this, when she saw her husband and cousin bathed in blood. She avoided telling her husband, however. The hour was not long in coming, when at 11 in the morning perpetrator and victim met on the stairs. The tenants realised that Nikolatos was going up to disturb Androniki again. He apparently thought her husband was at work, forgetting that the specific day was a public holiday. The two men exchanged looks of hatred.
'What do you want here?'
'Whatever I feel like...' He uttered a coarse word and added immediately: 'I'll take your wife whatever you do.'

Then Mazarakis lost his temper and as soon as he saw the victim reach toward his back pocket where he kept the bludgeon with which he had struck him the previous time, he drew his revolver and fired 4 times. The first bullet struck him near the groin, another in the head, the third in the chest and the fourth in the right leg.

He fell to the ground and made a last effort to lunge at Mazarakis while on the ground. Due to the shots, a crowd gathered and police officers arrived at the spot. The perpetrator went upstairs toward his home and announced to his wife:
'I've wounded the scoundrel!'

Androniki, in a state of frenzy, went onto the balcony. At that moment she saw the victim being carried by officers and, as the neighbours testify, when he saw her — despite the state he was in — he raised his hand, bit it, and stared at her threateningly.

He then fell into a state of aphasia during transfer to the Civic Hospital. Whether he will survive is uncertain. Mazarakis surrendered to the officers. Both to them, and at the 6th precinct where he was transferred, he stated: 'There was no other way, and patience has its limits. I have a saintly wife and he had made it his goal to dishonour her.' He repeated the same thing to the prosecutor, while Androniki, who has not stopped weeping, intuits that her husband is in the right and will not face a heavy sentence.

articles.title: Meliki, Imathia — The Anastenaria that Led to Matricide in the Village 1940
articles.author: Ακρόπολις
articles.excerpt: The ban on the Anastenaria in Meliki, Imathia, following the horrific matricide by an Anastenarissa. Bacchic rituals, fire-walking and the intervention of the authorities.

content.value: THESSALONIKI, 18 (From our correspondent)

The Veria authorities have banned the holding of the Anastenaria festivities, which were to take place on the feast day of Saint Constantine in the village of Meliki, in the presence of the president of the Society for Psychical Research, Mr. Tanagras.

The ban was imposed following the matricide by Despina Beza, who is an Anastenarissa and who, owing to the state of ecstasy that the initiates fall into during these festivities, had reached a state of madness when she killed her mother under the hair-raising circumstances I transmitted to you yesterday.
But what are these 'Anastenaria', which are performed in the village of Meliki in the Veria district and which are considered a continuation of the ancient Bacchic mysteries of Dionysus?

Those who perform them are called Anastenarians, and they celebrate with drums and clamour, sacrificing bulls and sheep as the ancient initiates of the Bacchic rituals of Dionysus did, and they dance on fire with bare feet without being burned.

These Anastenarians are sought by the Society for Psychical Research, and they were indeed found in Meliki. They came from the village of Kosti, one of the Greek villages of Bulgaria near the Black Sea, where this peculiar Christian-Dionysiac festivity used to be held, during which the fakir-like phenomenon of imperviousness to pain is repeated.

Mr. Tanagras discovered them with great effort, as those initiated into these rituals — both the Anastenarians and the villagers — are entrusted to keep this most ancient custom of the Dionysiac cult secret.

The Anastenarians of Meliki spoke to Mr. Tanagras about their custom. Of the old Anastenarians from the village of Kosti, in Meliki today there are: Kyra Despina Papazolina, an old woman of 60, Despina Beza the matricide, and Afendra Gousi.
These had as their chief Anastenarian a man by the name of Theodorakellis, who died and was succeeded in his office by Konstantinos Savvas.
There is also in Meliki the lyra player, the so-called Sevntalis, named Giorgios Petikopoylos, who played his lyra when the ritual was performed.
After the relocation of the inhabitants of the village of Kosti to Meliki, they continued to perform the Anastenaria ritual secretly and inside their homes.
The ritual was to be observed by Mr. Tanagras on the feast day of Saint Constantine, but was banned by the Veria authorities following the matricide.
HOW THE MATRICIDE OCCURRED
Beza, in the night from last Thursday to Friday, went to the room where her mother slept and asked her to light the fire.
The old woman, who was semi-paralysed, refused. Then Despina woke her son Giorgios, aged 13, who lit the fire.
Despina embraced her mother and began to hit her in the abdomen until she was left unconscious. She dragged her body toward the fire and turned her head so that the flames would touch her hair.
She removed her mother's clothes and her own, and doused both bodies with cold water.

The unfortunate old woman expired in terrible agony. Despina, no longer in full possession of her faculties, removed the clothes from her two children, Giorgios and Vasileios, and covered them with white sheets.
Then they all began to pray, having first painted black crosses on the walls of the room.
When dawn came, the matricide went out into the streets shouting: 'I killed my mother because she had the Archdevil inside her and so I saved Greece.'

articles.title: Were the 2 Bodies in Siteia Victims of Human Sacrifice? - 1995
articles.excerpt: An Italian couple was found dead on Christmas Eve in the coastal area of Faneromeni, Siteia. Beside the burned-out car, documents with occult content and implements of black magic were found, while the authorities do not rule out the possibility of human sacrifice.

image.alt: Archival image of the 1995 Adesmeutos Typos newspaper article, p. 24

content.value: A veil of mystery covers a crime in Siteia. An Italian couple was found on the night of Christmas Eve in the coastal area of Faneromeni, at Platani-Skopi. A man and a woman tied together and thrown onto the sharp rocks.

The disfigured bodies were discovered by dock worker Manolis Vasilakis, who alerted the Siteia Port Authority, which arranged for them to be transported by boat to the Venizeleio Hospital in Heraklion.

According to the forensic scientist for Crete, Mr. Manolis Frangoulis, the death of the 2 Italians — whose identities have not been made public — was due to severe injuries from the fall onto the rocks and must have occurred 2 days earlier.

The authorities do not rule out the possibility that they are faced with a human sacrifice by some sect. Beside the burned-out vehicle, damaged documents with occult content were found, while the man had a medallion with strange symbols around his neck.

It should be noted that yesterday afternoon, a few metres below the rocks, inside a cave, implements of black magic were found. Also at the bottom of the coastal area of Faneromeni, a travel bag was located with the number 666 engraved on it and titles of musical groups associated with Satanism.
G. Spyropoulos

articles.title: The Spousal Murder of Grocer Vastardis and the Witches - 1924
articles.excerpt: The crime of murdering a grocer in Ampelokipoi by his wife and her lover, with prior visits to witches for the destruction of the husband, highlights the morbid relationship between superstition and criminality.

image.alt: Archival image of the 1924 Ethnos newspaper article

content.value: The terrible drama of the murder of the poor grocer in Ampelokipoi is the most indicative example of the morbid criminality of the age. From what is gradually coming to light, we learn astounding details.

How the amorous passion of an elderly woman — if we are to believe the testimony of her lover — drove her to such a terrible crime that she was blinded to the point of preparing the murder with the same calm with which she was frying her meatballs. The intervention of the witches gives the crime the character of a true tragedy.

As is well known, in such cases witches are never absent; their invocation is considered indispensable for the commission of crimes. And how much superstition burdens our age is attested by the repeated visits of the two lovers to witches, with the aim of achieving the destruction of the husband, who was an obstacle to their amorous pleasures.

People still believe, even in the 20th century, that it is possible to destroy a man through sorcery and exorcisms. So imagine how much business these secret witches have in a city as large as Athens today. Besides the cartomancers and coffee-cup readers — whose clientele is often as large as that of dentists — there are also witches and sorcerers who, for a few hundred drachmas, undertake to invoke the spirits and demons against certain persons. How much ignorance exists in the midst of Athens, when even in the villages there are not many who believe in spells.

Fortunately, the demons of sorcerers and witches are not willing to commit murders, because otherwise there would not be a living person left in Athens and Piraeus. At least, if Vastardis and her lover had confined themselves to the intervention of witches, they would not have resorted to the knife, from which a good citizen and devoted husband fell dead.

However, even on this path we see human stupidity accompanied by savagery. The two lovers committed premeditated murder of the grocer with such recklessness that they were discovered from the first moment, if we accept at least the incriminating evidence announced up to now.

They believed that the grocer's murder would be explained as a robbery killing and they would remain at peace to continue their amorous tenderness. They did not count on the neighbours' suspicions, nor on the previous amorous episodes, which were enough to draw the authorities' attention to them immediately.
They believed that it sufficed for the grocer to disappear.

All such crimes are committed with recklessness, which also provides the measure of the passion driving them. What types are these. The lover: a husband with a beautiful wife and a daughter of marriageable age. His mistress: another man's wife, with many children and also a daughter of marriageable age. Her unfortunate husband provided her with all comforts and she had never known hardship. Yet neither conjugal devotion, nor maternal affection, nor even her advanced age were sufficient to keep her on the path of virtue.

But the mad Medea slaughtered her children, whereas Vastardis confined herself merely to slaughtering her husband. Of course, such criminal types are only exceptions, but recently they are showing an increase and multiplying. They constitute a branch of the great criminality of our age.
If the guilt of this elderly woman is confirmed, then we are faced with a terrible criminal type that induces vertigo.
